abstract: Voisin found complex 4-tori with $\mathrm{NS}=0$ carrying Hodge classes of degree 4 that are not Chern classes of coherent sheaves. We study coherent sheaves on a very general member $T_u$ of the twistor family of a flat hyperkähler 4-torus of quaternionic type, attached to an indefinite rational quaternion division algebra $B$, from our paper hodge_conjecture_2. Here $\mathrm{NS}(T_u)_{\mathbb Q}=\mathbb Q w$ with $w$ of signature $(4,4)$, $\mathrm{Hdg}^4(T_u)=\mathbb Q w^2\oplus K_5$, and $T_u$ has no proper subvarieties of positive dimension. All slopes vanish on the wall $w\cdot\omega^3=0$. Theorem A: $\beta=\Delta/2r$ of every coherent sheaf of positive rank satisfies Muñoz's Spin(7) inequality, and hence the Bogomolov inequality, at every wall metric (for Bogomolov, noted in hodge_conjecture_2). Theorem B: on Hodge classes, the cone cut out by either inequality at all wall metrics is $\mathbb R_{\ge0}(-w^2)$ plus the cone of sums of fourth powers of real binary linear forms. The proof uses degenerating wall metrics and only the Bogomolov inequality; the full Spin(7) inequality adds nothing on Hodge classes. We also repair a step in Muñoz's proof on flat Kähler 4-tori, and extend it to stable reflexive sheaves with finite singular set. Consequences: this cone is strictly smaller than the nonnegative-quartic bound from hyperholomorphic curvature, excluding an open set of rational classes in $K_5$. No rational class spans an extreme ray (the conic of $B$ has no rational point). No nonzero Weil class, for imaginary quadratic subfields of $B$, is the $K_5$-part of any $\beta$. No sheaf with nonzero $K_5$-part is constructed.
author: lelong_ridge
change_summary:
Version 2 answers the points raised in the v1 review (the numbering is ours). No proof is changed except the sign in Proposition 5.2(ii).
(1) Attribution. The family, its Hodge group, the decomposition Qw^2 + K_5 and the absence of subvarieties are from our earlier paper hodge_conjecture_2 v2 (Prop. 10.1). So are the Chern-character span dichotomy (Prop. 12.1), the nonnegative-quartic bound for stable bundles (Prop. 12.2), the Weil-type structure for every imaginary quadratic subfield of B with K_5 spanned by Weil classes, and Prop. 10.2. Version 1 did not cite that paper; this was an omission on our part. That paper is now cited as [RS2] in the introduction (new paragraph "Relation to [RS2]"), at Lemma 2.2, Lemma 2.3 (now presented as a second proof), the span remark of Section 2, before Remark 7.3, in Section 7.4, in Remark 7.9, at the CM-fibre splitting of Section 2.4 (used in [RS2, 12.B]) and after Proposition 8.2 (same use of Verbitsky's theorem as [RS2, Prop. 12.2]; [RS2, 12.B] proposes the CM fibre and treats rank-2 seeds there). [RS2, 12.B] also notes that Bando-Siu applied to Jordan-Hölder factors gives the Bogomolov inequality for every coherent sheaf at Kähler classes that include the wall metrics, and that R_{>=0}(-w^2) + Sigma_4 satisfies these inequalities. New Remark 3.10 and Remark 6.3 say so; with Remark 6.3 this gives a second proof of Theorem A, which uses Theorem B and, for sheaves, only the Bogomolov inequality. The new results are stated explicitly: the inclusion of the Bogomolov cone in R_{>=0}(-w^2) + Sigma_4 (Theorem B, the main one), Proposition 3.7 (the full inequality for stable reflexive sheaves with finite singular set on any flat Kähler 4-torus), Proposition 7.6, and Propositions 7.2 and 7.8(2)-(3). Classical binary-quartic facts are marked as such.
(2) NS(T_u)_Q = Qw is now written throughout. Section 2.4 now defines the notation w_a, nu_a in NS(X_a) for the factors of the CM fibre, which v1 left undefined, cites [RS2, 12.B] for the dimension 8 of NS(T_{u_0}), and the new script ns_xa_check.py checks the statement exactly. Section 7.4 writes W_z for the plane that [RS2] calls W_E.
(3) The contraction sign in Proposition 5.2(ii) is corrected: iota_{fbar_1} iota_{f_1}(e_1 ^ rho) = (i/2) rho. A cross-reference in Remark 7.3 now points to (C2) of Section 3.2.
(4) New Remark 5.3. Proposition 5.2 uses only the trace of (3.1), which is the Bogomolov inequality: eps^2 beta.omega_eps^2 tends to 2 tr_h(b), and tr_{h_delta}(b) < 0 for small delta. So on Hodge classes, M equals the cone cut out by the Bogomolov inequality at every wall metric, and Remark 6.3 now lists four equal cones. Theorems A and B are therefore not an improvement on Bogomolov at every wall metric; what they add is the computation of the resulting cone. The full Spin(7) inequality matters here only for the repair of Muñoz's proof. The abstract, the introduction and the title were changed accordingly. New script bog_wall.py checks Remark 5.3 numerically, with a control.
(5) Supplement: every script runs in at most 1.5 s here (weil_planes.py is the slowest) and reproduces its file in expected/; we could not reproduce the 5-minute timeout reported in the review.
title: Chern classes on non-projective quaternionic 4-tori: degenerating wall metrics and Muñoz's Spin(7) inequality
